summary: Iter164 — feature test for new action_type (task/standing_commitment) + trigger classification. Backend pytest suite (7/7 pass) via test_action_type_standing_commitment.py exercising PUT /review/{id}/actions round-trip for task, standing_commitment, and legacy-typeless actions; literal 'Not specified in session' due_date persisted verbatim; PATCH toggle-complete works for both types; GET /admin/team-insights/registers passes action_type + trigger through and never leaks a truthy due_date on standing commitments (so the sort/overdue bucket cannot flag them); export-pdf returns valid application/pdf on a signed-off meeting; unit test on utils.ai._sanitise_analysis confirms missing/invalid action_type defaults to 'task' AND the literal 'Not specified in session' string is preserved (not swallowed by the nullish set). Frontend UI test (Playwright, main flow): Task pill selected by default on '+ Add Action' with due input, Standing pill click swaps to trigger input, both types save + render correctly (row 0 Task shows 'Due: 2026-02-20' with no Standing badge, row 1 Standing shows indigo 'Standing' badge + 'Trigger: any time this comes up'); tooltips verified — task shows 'Mark as complete' → 'Mark as outstanding', standing shows 'Close' → 'Reopen' after toggle; edit form flips a task to a standing commitment with the trigger input replacing the due date input, saves cleanly, and the row re-renders with the Standing badge + 'Trigger: regression-check trigger'. Test fixture meeting fbeb47d0-bf87-43ba-99bb-8e7388ecb238 left with an empty actions array as requested.
critical_code_review_comments: admin.py _reg_sort_registers (line 1555-1558) buckets 'overdue' based on `a['due_date'] and a['due_date'] < today`. For standing commitments the whitelist at line 1481 normalises due_date to '' (empty string) which is falsy → correctly not overdue. Verified in test_team_insights_passthrough_and_no_overdue_for_standing. This works today but is subtle — if anyone ever changes the whitelist default to None-vs-'' inconsistently, a standing commitment with a stale due_date on the underlying JSONB (e.g. from a legacy row that was edited from task→standing without clearing due_date) would appear as 'Overdue'. Consider explicitly excluding action_type=='standing_commitment' in the overdue filter as a defensive belt-and-braces (mirror what TeamInsights.js line 670/868 already does client-side).

The PDF export column header string 'Due Date / Trigger' is duplicated across backend (review.py:2263) and TeamInsights.js CSV (line 905). Fine for now, but a shared constant would prevent divergence later.

AI-generated action_type from a live transcript was NOT exercised end-to-end (would require a fresh recording + full pipeline run — expensive and slow). The prompt in ai.py lines 530-531/647-650 is well-specified and _sanitise_analysis at line 262-263 provides a hard safety net (any bad or missing value defaults to 'task'), so the frontend cannot crash on legacy/malformed AI output. Main-agent may want to spot-check one live analysis with an open-ended commitment phrase separately.

Rollover-of-standing-commitment behaviour was NOT re-executed (code path in utils/transcription_pipeline.py is unchanged from tasks — same is_rolled_over/source_meeting_title mechanism; would need a fresh meeting to trigger). Since the flexible-JSONB action shape now includes action_type/trigger fields and the carry-forward simply copies the dict forward, functional correctness is high-confidence; visual correctness in the carried row already covered by badge/trigger rendering tests.
